properties.statement:
THE 'NEXT LEVER' HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG: build_network's per-node edge scan is NOT the dominant cost of the defect scan, and fixing it did not move loop_status or detect_defects after a write. Recorded because the optimize skill says to expect falsified hypotheses and record them so the next session does not re-run this one.

WHAT WAS BUILT (perf/one-pass-edge-read, NOT committed as of this fact): a real O(N)->O(1) fix. `build_network_of` gathered edges with one `self.outgoing(id, None)` STORE PREFIX-SCAN PER NODE (~3,700 scans); `all_edges_of_type` did the same per node, per type, across ~8 callers. Both now consume a single `scan_all_edges(graph_id)` — a prefix scan of CF_ADJ_OUT over the graph prefix, which returns every edge in one pass in (from,type,to) key order, the SAME order the per-node loop produced concatenated, so determinism is preserved by construction. All 1,578 core tests and 343 mcp tests pass unchanged, which is the proof the community assignments and defects are byte-identical.

MEASURED, release, live-store copy, medians of 4 write->call boundaries, load ~1.8:
  loop_status after a write:    6,354 -> 7,039 ms   (budget 2,000)   NOT MOVED
  detect_defects after a write: 5,633 -> 5,817 ms                    NOT MOVED
Both within noise of baseline. The change did not meet its budget.

⭐ THE HYPOTHESIS THAT WAS FALSIFIED, stated so it is not retried: 'build_network's per-node edge scan is the ~5 s.' The debug phase-probe had shown design_network at 1.56 s debug (~0.4 s release) — a FRACTION, not the bulk. I over-read a distributed cost as a single hot spot, and then briefly mis-read a MEMO HIT (detect_defects 2,716 ms reusing a prior scan) as the optimization working. On a quiet machine with medians and a real write between calls (which invalidates the memo and forces the scan), the win vanishes.

⭐ WHERE THE COST ACTUALLY IS, still not isolated in release: the debug split was pre-structural per-type detectors 8.35 s (35%), structural 4.6 s (design_network 1.56 + clusters 0.53 + operational_network 0.63 + circular_dependencies 1.82), sweep_scope + ack filter ~11 s (46%, detect_defects-only). The one-pass change touched only the 1.56 + 0.63 network builds. The pre-structural per-type detectors and circular_dependencies were NOT touched and are the larger share. To move loop_status, the next investigation must release-profile all_defects' per-type detector loop — which walks nodes and reads properties/edges per node — not the network build.

🛑 WHAT IS UNDECIDED AND IS ANTHONY'S CALL: whether to ship the one-pass change at all. It is CORRECT and removes a genuine O(N) redundancy (a bulk edge reader is a primitive reflow2 lacked), it helps debug/test time, and it has no downside — but it moves no release budget, so it is a tidiness win, not a latency win. Shipping a correct-but-not-budget-moving change is a prioritisation question the skill assigns to the person, not the loop. The merged multiplier fix (#428) remains the real session-level win; this is separate and smaller.

BOUNDS: one machine, 4 cores, release, stdio, live-store copy, load 1.8-5 across the window; medians of 4. The determinism claim rests on the full test suite passing, not on a diff of outputs.
